clue.text: Benign girl' can: put back the calendar.

parts.note: Alma is a girl's name and the Latin for kindly or nourishing, as in alma mater

indicators.note: putting a word back means writing its letters in the reverse order

explanation.surface: A kind young woman returns a tin together with the year's calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns CAN into NAC, which follows ALMA.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a yearly publication built around a calendar of dates, tides and festivals.

clue.text: Neath's strangely full of classic sightseers

indicators.note: something done strangely is out of its normal order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the town name Neath with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: The Welsh town of Neath is unexpectedly crowded with tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: Neath is a town in South Wales; here its S counts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek capital is packed with visitors to the Parthenon and other ancient ruins.

clue.text: Where Napoleon made his horse go around north?

definitions.text: Where Napoleon made his horse go around north?

parts.words: Where Napoleon made his horse go around north
parts.note: the battle in northern Italy where Napoleon won in 1800, also the name of the grey horse he rode

explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon's horse was named after his victory over the Austrians in Piedmont, northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1800 battle site in Piedmont and Napoleon's famous Arab stallion share the name.

clue.text: Novices get involved in, phoney set-up

indicators.note: letters that get involved are mixed up together into a new order

explanation.surface: Beginners get drawn into a fraudulent scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get involved in' mixes PHONEY and SET; 'up' finishes the surface phrase 'set-up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a beginner or newly admitted convert.

clue.text: A summons people get: after making a scene

definitions.text: A summons people get: after making a scene

parts.words: A summons people get: after making a scene
parts.note: actors called back before the audience after playing a scene, not people summoned for causing a fuss

explanation.definitionFit: Performers are called out in front of the lowered stage drape to take applause at the end of a show.

clue.text: Speculation' of a florin 'at first, say

indicators.note: tells us the florin's letters stand at the front of the answer

parts.note: fl. is the standard abbreviation for florin, a coin
to say something is to utter it

explanation.surface: Someone talks of gambling a two-shilling coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A florin was an old British two-shilling coin, abbreviated FL.
explanation.definitionFit: A flutter is British slang for a small bet or speculative gamble.

parts.note: having eaten enough, with a meal sitting in the stomach

explanation.definitionFit: Someone given a meal has been nourished until full.

clue.text: As for the Customs, this. one put years on us.

definitions.note: plural in the clue while the answer is a mass noun covering habits in general

parts.note: us is taken as written
age is a span of years

explanation.surface: A remark about Customs officers, whose dealings age us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put years on us' means add AGE to US.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means established practice or habit, the way things are customarily done.

clue.text: Heroine has time' to help. form a mosaic

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Hardy's heroine
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A heroine has spare time to assist with a mosaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small tiles that together make up a mosaic.

parts.note: the patter song in Ruddigore says this particularly rapid unintelligible patter isn't generally heard

explanation.walkthrough: W. S. Gilbert wrote the words of Gilbert and Sullivan operas; the 'Matter' trio in Ruddigore sings of 'this particularly rapid, unintelligible patter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed is what makes a patter song hard to follow, and the lyric itself names it.

clue.text: Abhorred universal upheaval, so took shelter

indicators.note: an upheaval throws things into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Widespread turmoil that people detested drove them to seek refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour can mean, in an older sense, to lodge or take refuge somewhere.

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the words are read from end to start

explanation.surface: A preacher of morals adopts a backward-looking stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrograde' reads POSE A backwards; 'assumed' only completes the picture of a pose being taken up.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek storyteller whose fables each end with a moral lesson.

clue.text: A date for some Roamin in the Gloamin'

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are taken, a run lying across them

explanation.surface: A day chosen for wandering through the Scottish dusk, as in the old song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roamin' in the Gloamin'' is a Harry Lauder music-hall song; the letters run across 'Roamin in the'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth is a day of the month, so it names a date on the calendar.

explanation.surface: Grasping how someone could dread being taken into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp, to dread and to seize by law are all senses of the same verb, as apprehension shows.

parts.note: pop as slang for father, so a festival for pop, though it sounds like loud music dads may not enjoy

explanation.definitionFit: A rock music event outdoors is a festival of popular music, and pop is also a word for dad.

parts.note: a countryman who writes verse is both rhymer and farm worker, and Franz von Suppé wrote a famous overture with that title

explanation.walkthrough: Suppé was a 19th-century Austrian composer of light operas and overtures.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Suppé's operetta pairs a rhymer with a country labourer, which is a rustic versifier.

parts.note: an instrument whose bellows fold and unfold, not a file holding sheet music

explanation.definitionFit: The squeezebox's pleated bellows fold in and out to make the music.

indicators.note: letters put around are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A fence is set up around a seat at the dock.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade is a defensive enclosure or barrier of upright stakes.

parts.note: something guileless is see-through in character, and slides for a projector are see-through films

explanation.definitionFit: Projector slides are see-through photographic films, and an ingenuous person is see-through in nature.

parts.note: a.m. means before noon, early in the day

indicators.note: one piece takes in the other, which ends up inside it

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A morning tendency takes in someone who goes for a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes something surrounding or encompassing on all sides.

clue.text: 'To 'save 'up I have to be a bit deceitful

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone admits that to put money aside they must be slightly dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SAVE into EVAS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Being evasive means dodging the truth, a mildly dishonest habit.

explanation.surface: A passenger gets on the buses.
explanation.definitionFit: The boards of a theatre are its platforms, and stagecoaches were horse-drawn coaches.

clue.text: The car's a hindrance after taking a hired one to Rio

definitions.note: read as 'the car is', so it defines a noun

indicators.note: the hindrance is placed after the other pieces

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle hired for a journey
a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance' and a let in tennis

explanation.surface: A hold-up occurs after someone takes a taxi to Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a convertible motor car, originally a light horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Such a view may lead-to an engagement:

definitions.text: Such a view may lead-to an engagement

parts.words: Such a view may lead-to an engagement
parts.note: put this word before view to make a job ..., which can end in being hired

explanation.definitionFit: The word joined to view gives a job meeting that may result in being taken on, an engagement.

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together in a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The Astor hotel has been reconstructed, and what a building it is!
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a joint of meat cooked in the oven.

parts.note: vert is the heraldic term for green

explanation.surface: An instruction to steer clear of a coat-of-arms tint.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert is to ward off or prevent something from happening.

parts.note: Salome's dance of the seven veils strips them off one by one, the same act as uncovering a statue at a formal opening

explanation.definitionFit: A formal ceremony revealing a new statue or plaque involves removing its veil, as Salome's dance did.

indicators.note: the river's letters lie inside the answer to clue 9

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire bloom found inside another answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, and a flower is crossword slang for something that flows.

explanation.surface: A flute player who is one of a group of nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Euterpe, Muse of music and lyric poetry, is shown playing the flute, and the Muses numbered nine.

explanation.surface: Mounted soldiers performing a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancer regiments were mounted troops with lances, and the lancers is also a 19th-century square dance like a quadrille.
